relevant_laws.name: Bénéfices Industriels et Commerciaux (BIC)
relevant_laws.description: This is the category under which LMNP rental income is taxed in France. Taxpayers can opt for either the micro-BIC regime (simplified with a flat-rate allowance) or the real regime (deducting actual expenses).

relevant_laws.name: Micro-BIC Regime
relevant_laws.description: A simplified tax regime for LMNP where a flat-rate allowance of 50% (or 71% for classified tourist accommodation) is deducted from rental income before taxation. This applies as long as annual rents do not exceed €70,000 (€170,000 for classified tourist accommodation).

relevant_laws.name: Simplified Real Regime (Régime Réel)
relevant_laws.description: An LMNP tax option allowing landlords to deduct actual expenses incurred in relation to the rental activity, such as repairs, maintenance, interest on loans, and crucially, depreciation of the property and furniture. This often results in a lower taxable income compared to the micro-BIC regime.

statistics: Under the micro-BIC regime, a 50% allowance is applied to rental income, increasing to 71% for classified furnished tourist accommodation.
Annual rental income must generally be below €70,000 to qualify for LMNP, or €170,000 for classified tourist accommodations.
key_facts: The LMNP (Loueur en Meublé Non Professionnel) status is for individuals renting out furnished properties who do not meet the criteria for professional status.
LMNP rental income is taxed under Bénéfices Industriels et Commerciaux (BIC – Industrial and Commercial Profits).
Taxpayers can choose between the micro-BIC regime (a flat-rate allowance) or the simplified real regime (deducting actual expenses).
Under the micro-BIC regime, a 50% allowance is applied to rental income. This increases to 71% for properties classified as furnished tourist accommodation.
The simplified real regime (Régime Réel) allows for the deduction of actual expenses, including property depreciation, furniture, and major renovations, which can significantly reduce taxable income.
For LMNP status, annual rental income must generally be below €70,000, or €170,000 for classified tourist accommodations.

Previously, for non-residents, the LMNP/LMP (Loueur en Meublé Professionnel) status determination often excluded foreign income, potentially classifying them under LMP even if it wasn't their primary activity.
Changes are being implemented regarding how non-residents' LMNP/LMP status is determined, with a move towards considering worldwide income.
The LMNP scheme is considered attractive for foreign investors due to its tax benefits, including expense deductions and favorable treatment upon resale.
